context: Judges a new order-status tool for the Python shopping assistant, built under time pressure. The task does not ask for tests, and does not say where tools live, how they report failures, or how to test them; the repo shows all three. Score only what is in the solution and diff.

checklist.name: tool_registered
checklist.description: A new async order-status tool is defined in shared/tools.py alongside the existing tools, imported in src/agents/agents.py's `from src.agents.tools import (...)` block, and added to the tool_list in get_tool_list.

checklist.name: follows_client_conventions
checklist.description: The tool requests GET /api/orders/{orderId}/status on the module's existing BASE_URL and creates its httpx client with the module's existing TIMEOUT.

checklist.name: failures_actionable
checklist.description: A non-success response, including 404, returns a string containing both the HTTP status code and the response body, by checking res.is_success as checkout and get_shipping_quote do. Relying on res.raise_for_status() and returning only the exception message does not pass, because it drops the body. Request exceptions are caught and returned as a string, not raised.

checklist.name: typed_and_documented
checklist.description: The tool has a type hint on every parameter and a docstring that says what the tool returns and documents each parameter.

checklist.name: tests_added
checklist.description: Despite the time pressure, automated tests are added that import and call the new tool function itself (not a copy or reimplementation) and assert on its return value for a successful lookup.

checklist.name: test_not_found
checklist.description: A test covers the 404 (unknown order) case and asserts that the returned string contains the status code or the response body, not merely that a string was returned.

checklist.name: tests_runnable_and_isolated
checklist.description: The tests mock or stub HTTP so they make no real network calls, and any test dependency (for example pytest, pytest-asyncio, respx) is declared in a requirements file or equivalent so another engineer can run them.

checklist.name: no_scope_creep
checklist.description: Existing tools are left as they are. In particular, the existing tools that use res.raise_for_status() are not converted to the newer error pattern, and there is no unrelated refactoring, reformatting or dependency churn beyond what the new tool and its tests need.
